observations: The routine touches no memory: 0 loads and 0 stores across the 26 non-nop instructions; verify.py raises if any instruction carries a memory operand.
The return is a std::pair<int,int> packed into the single INTEGER eightbyte rax (low dword first field, high dword second), formed by shl $0x20 + or at 0x5dd5f29/0x5dd5f2d.
kDefault (-1) in the flush argument alone does not start the derivation: 0x5dd5f3d requires the compaction argument to be -1 as well.

When the flush argument is -1 but the compaction argument is explicit, flushes becomes 1 (eax is seeded with 1 at 0x5dd5f38 and the jal at 0x5dd5f40 rejoins the explicit path): kDefault clamps exactly like a non-positive value.
multi_db = false forces the compaction count to 1 even on the derived path: the derived pair jumps back (0x5dd5f59) into the multi-db test at 0x5dd5f1d.
The derivation splits the job budget with a *signed* shift: flushes = jobs / 4 (sar $0x2) only when jobs > 7; at most seven jobs keeps a single flush.
The remainder is clamped with a signed compare (cmovle at 0x5dd5f56), so compactions = max(1, jobs - flushes) and a remainder that wrapped negative becomes 1.
At jobs = INT_MIN the subtraction wraps to INT_MAX and survives the clamp, i.e. the routine returns (1, 2147483647) for that input; the ledger keeps the row verbatim.

All four call sites consume the packed pair and each splits it itself: three with a signed shift (0x5d7268d, 0x5d72689, 0x5dfcef9) and one with an unsigned shift (0x5e5d00c); the two are equivalent only because both fields are small positive ints.
The function is a complete artifact body: 7 int3 bytes below the entry and 5 above the end, with no relocations and a raw-equal rebuilt source body.
unknowns: Which DBOptions field feeds each argument is an inference from the callers' load offsets plus the public rocksdb 8.1.1 source; the binary alone fixes the register roles.
Only four call sites exist in this artifact; other callers (if any exist in other builds) are outside this packet.
The multi_db = false branch has no observed caller here, so it is recovered by decoding only.
Two of the four call sites share one FDE (0x5d71fe0..0x5d72e50) and call the routine twice with different option offsets; this packet makes no claim about that function's identity.
The three identical source copies recorded by the vendor census (identical_source_count 3) are not enumerated individually here.
